actions.justification: Mandatory first action - assess vital signs to establish baseline and identify any hemodynamic instability. Patient has liver failure which requires careful monitoring.
Essential to identify the primary reason for presentation in order to guide clinical decision-making and appropriate workup for this patient with liver failure.
Assess overall clinical status including mental status and general appearance, particularly important in liver failure where hepatic encephalopathy and other complications may be present.
Patient has liver failure comorbidity; assessing mental status is critical to evaluate for hepatic encephalopathy, which can present with altered consciousness.
With known liver failure, abdominal assessment is essential to evaluate for signs of hepatomegaly, ascites, jaundice, or other hepatic complications.
Cardiovascular assessment helps identify any hemodynamic instability or complications related to liver failure such as hepatorenal syndrome or portal hypertension effects.
Patient has liver failure comorbidity; neurological assessment is critical to evaluate for hepatic encephalopathy, which is a common and serious complication in liver failure patients.
Liver failure patients are at risk for fluid imbalances, ascites, and electrolyte disturbances. Assessing hydration status is essential for guiding management.
Liver failure patients are immunocompromised and prone to infections such as spontaneous bacterial peritonitis (SBP). Identifying any infection source is a priority given the clinical context.
Comprehensive patient assessment to consolidate findings from individual system assessments and establish a working diagnosis, particularly important given liver failure comorbidity.
Patient has known liver failure; assessing for multi-organ dysfunction is critical to determine severity and guide management decisions.
Pain assessment has not yet been completed and is essential for identifying the chief complaint's severity and guiding further workup.
Patient with liver failure is at risk for hepatopulmonary syndrome and pleural effusions; respiratory assessment is warranted.
Liver failure carries significant risk of hepatorenal syndrome; monitoring urine output is critical for early detection of renal complications.
Skin assessment in liver failure can reveal jaundice, spider angiomas, palmar erythema, and signs of bleeding diathesis, aiding clinical staging.

Patient has liver failure comorbidity - comprehensive musculoskeletal assessment to check for hepatic encephalopathy-related muscle changes, asterixis, or other manifestations not yet captured in completed assessments.

Patient has liver failure - baseline renal function (eGFR) is critical to assess for hepatorenal syndrome and guide medication dosing. Renal function is closely linked to outcomes in liver failure patients.
Patient with liver failure requires hepatology/gastroenterology specialist consultation to guide management, assess severity (Child-Pugh/MELD score), and determine appropriate level of care.
Patient has liver failure comorbidity; establishing IV access is essential for fluid administration, medication delivery, and further workup. Stable vitals allow time for this foundational step.
Neurological assessment scoring (NIHSS) has not been completed and is important given the patient's liver failure which can cause hepatic encephalopathy affecting neurological status.
Patient with liver failure comorbidity requires hospital admission for monitoring and further workup regardless of current stable vitals, as liver failure patients can decompensate rapidly.
